claims.text: Lightweight high-entropy alloys with atomic-size mismatch δ below 6% form and retain a single-phase solid solution.
Retention of a single-phase solid solution refines grain size.
The refined grain size enhances mechanical strength.
A single-phase solid solution maintains uniformly distributed Al and Cr.
Uniformly distributed Al and Cr form continuous protective oxide scales and passive films.
The proposed microstructure enables low density, high strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance to be combined.
Equiatomic Ti-V-Cr-Al-Nb can be engineered to have δ below 6% in the as-cast, homogenized condition.
Substituting 5 at.% Ti with 5 at.% Cr raises δ from below 6% to above 6%.
The Ti-to-Cr substitution leaves alloy density nearly unchanged.
High configurational entropy at δ below 6% suppresses intermetallic formation.
High configurational entropy at δ below 6% stabilizes fine grains.
When δ exceeds 6%, phase separation and intermetallic precipitation coarsen the microstructure.
Intermetallic formation above δ of 6% embrittles the alloy.
Phase separation above δ of 6% depletes Al and Cr and thereby degrades corrosion and oxidation resistance.
The δ-below-6% alloy will have at least 10% higher yield strength than the δ-above-6% alloy.
The δ-below-6% alloy will have at least 20% higher hardness than the δ-above-6% alloy.
The δ-below-6% alloy will have at least 50% lower corrosion current density in 3.5 wt% NaCl.
The δ-below-6% alloy will have at least 30% lower oxide weight gain after 100 hours at 1000 °C in air.
Above approximately 1200 °C, rapid grain growth and oxide-scale breakdown occur regardless of δ.
In highly aggressive halide-rich environments such as HCl vapor, pitting overrides δ-dependent passive-film stability.

contradictions.description: Lower corrosion current density and lower oxidation weight gain are predicted to indicate better performance, but the falsification rule says the δ>6% alloy matching or exceeding the δ<6% alloy in these quantities would falsify the hypothesis. Exceeding them means higher corrosion current and higher weight gain, which is worse performance and is consistent with, rather than contrary to, the prediction.

The intervention says density is kept nearly constant, whereas the baseline describes the two compositions as having identical density. Exact identity is stronger than and not established by the stated near-constancy.
